newsitem.title: GERMANY: Volkswagen jobs plan draws fire, praise.
newsitem.headline: Volkswagen jobs plan draws fire, praise.

text.p: Auto maker Volkswagen AG's plans to set up an internal agency for short-time workers on Thursday drew criticism from unions and praise from politicians who said it could help create jobs.
The DGB Federation of German Trade Unions on Thursday sharply criticised the plan, saying it would allow VW to circumvent its wage agreement, which pays workers more than the industry-wide pact.
"We will do everything we can to hinder this undermining of contracts aimed at lowering wages," DGB wage specialist Reinhard Dombre said in a televised interview.
VW confirmed it was discussing with unions a plan to set up such a subsidiary in an effort to cut costs, but it declined to disclose details.
Dombre said other major companies are also contemplating similar plans. Labour unrest could result if employers pay workers different wages for doing the same job, he said.

Engineering union IG Metall said the company planned to pay the temporary workers less under the industry-wide contract. But Bernd Sudholt, deputy leader of VW's works council, said the company would pay workers in the new unit according to its house contract.
He suggested the company could cut costs by hiring more workers under term contracts, which pay no holiday bonuses or other special payments.
Hermann-Josef Arentz, a Christian Democratic Union (CDU) official responsible for jobs, told Germany's Express newspaper the plan was a positive development if it helped create jobs.

"The offer is a good one, if it leads to the creation of more jobs rather than overtime, and more than could be created at VW wages," Arentz said. But he warned VW only to embark on such a plan with the cooperation of its union.

Mannheim University economics professor Wolfgang Franz, an advisor to Chancellor Helmut Kohl, said such plans are likely to become more common as companies try to work more flexibly to even out the peaks and troughs of production cycles.
